questions.q: Learning is often seen as the contiguous causal effect of ____ on behavior.
questions.explanation: Learning is defined as a relatively permanent change in behavior or behavior potential that results from experience. Trauma can affect behavior, but the general causal factor in learning is experience.

questions.q: In order to say that learning has occurred, a hidden change in behavior must occur.
questions.explanation: Learning is inferred from an observable (overt) change in behavior or performance, not a hidden one. A change that cannot be observed in any way cannot be used to say learning has occurred.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a mental construct?
questions.explanation: Knowledge, representations and associations are hypothetical mental constructs used to explain learning. A skeleton is a physical, anatomical structure, not a mental construct.

questions.q: Learning changes the ____ structure of the brain through the process of continuous interactions between the learner and the external environment.
questions.explanation: Learning physically alters the brain (neuroplasticity), for example by forming and strengthening synaptic connections through ongoing interaction with the environment.
Learning is influenced by both cognition (attention, beliefs, reasoning) and emotion (motivation, anxiety, interest), so neither alone fully shapes it.

questions.q: Watson's work included the famous Little Albert experiment in which he conditioned a small child to ____ a white rat.
questions.explanation: Watson and Rayner (1920) paired a white rat with a loud noise until Little Albert showed a conditioned fear response to the rat, demonstrating classical conditioning of emotions.

questions.q: Behaviorism dominated psychology for much of the early ____ century.
questions.explanation: Behaviorism, launched by Watson in 1913 and extended by Skinner, dominated psychology from roughly the 1910s to the 1950s, before the cognitive revolution.

questions.q: The state of "conscious incompetence" may be valuable ____ of a learning experience.
questions.explanation: In the conscious competence model, realizing what you do not know (conscious incompetence) motivates learning, so it is valuable at the start. Ending a learning experience still in this stage would indicate the learning failed.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an outcome of effective e-learning?
questions.explanation: Effective e-learning should produce more connected, integrated knowledge along with broader strategies, reflection and positive emotions. Disconnected knowledge is a sign of ineffective learning.

questions.q: Instrumental conditioning is an example of ____ learning.
questions.explanation: Instrumental (operant) conditioning involves learning an association between a behavior and its consequence, making it associative learning. Habituation and sensitization are non-associative forms of learning.
